Maria (Support): Heads-up — BrightGrove opened an escalation: spike of 429s + duplicate billing events after they ran a short internal load run this morning (~09:15 UTC). They say 3 API keys hit concurrently and token rotation started failing. They attached a tiny log snippet, paste below.

Jonah (Eng-SRE): Can you drop the sample logs and a minimal repro? Do we know if these are 429 vs 5xx? Also, which route/model was hit and approximate QPS?

Maria (Support): Logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T09:15:23Z INFO request_id=rc_9d token=key-*** status=429 route=/v1/generate latency_ms=210
2026-03-17T09:15:24Z INFO request_id=rc_9e token=key-*** status=200 route=/v1/generate latency_ms=180
2026-03-17T09:15:30Z INFO request_id=rc_a0 token=key-*** status=429 route=/v1/generate latency_ms=95
```
They say their internal canary ran ~4x expected steady QPS for ~90s and workers retried on 429 which caused billing noise. Minimal repro they ran locally: `hey -z 90s -q 200 -c 50 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` (they used 3 keys round-robin).

Arjun (Eng-Infra): Thanks — couple things to check: 1) token bucket bursting window and burst multiplier for per-key limits, 2) whether short-lived tokens were rotated mid-run (that can create auth churn and transient 401/429 behavior), 3) our request routing fallback behavior when a model node is saturated (we may return 429 quickly).

Jonah (Eng-SRE): Proposed repro plan (small, controlled):
1) Use a single test key and run a 3-phase attack: warmup (30s at steady qps), spike (60s at 4x steady), cooldown (30s).
2) Capture per-token metrics from Console + request traces (token_bucket.fill, consumed_tokens, route).
3) Run again with round-robin across 3 keys to reproduce retry/billing pattern.

Arjun (Eng-Infra): Example vegeta command to reproduce the spike (safe, controlled):
```
echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate","body":"{\"prompt\":\"test\"}","header":{"Authorization":"Bearer $TEST_KEY","Content-Type":"application/json"}}' | vegeta attack -duration=2m -rate=200 | tee results.bin | vegeta report
```
And a candidate per-key rate-limit config snippet we should test against (not a prod push):
```
{
  "per_key_qps": 2.0,             // steady qps per token
  "burst_multiplier": 5,         // how many extra requests allowed in burst window
  "burst_window_secs": 10,       // short window where bursts are absorbed
  "cooldown_secs": 30            // time to refill token bucket
}
```
My reasoning: a conservative steady qps + a short burst window cushions short spikes without opening a long tail that allows retries to cause billing spirals.

Sarah (Customer): Confirming — our canary was ~200 req/s for 90s, keys rotated every 45s by the orchestrator. We saw 401s during rotation and clients retried, then 429s. We can run the vegeta command if you give us a safe target rate and an IP allowlist for staging.

Jonah (Eng-SRE): Immediate steps I recommend we take now: 
- Ask BrightGrove to stop the ongoing internal run (if still active).
- Temporarily enable short-circuiting for retries for that org (increase retry backoff at SDK or gateway).
- Run the controlled repro in our staging with 1 key, then 3-key round-robin to confirm burst-induced billing pattern.
- Instrument: add a lightweight counter in request path for "billing_retry_trigger" (increments when a retry succeeds after 429).

Maria (Support): I'll open a support ticket with the repro plan and request BrightGrove run the staged vegeta with our guidance. Also will ask them for a CSV of affected request_ids/time windows.

OpsBot: Ticket #INC-2026-478 created by Maria (Support) — priority P2 — assigned to Jonah (Eng-SRE) and Arjun (Eng-Infra). https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-478 :white_check_mark:

Jonah (Eng-SRE): Quick note on defaults to validate in the lab: per-user default steady limit ~120 req/min (2 req/s) with a burst window allowing ~5x for up to 10s has historically avoided retry storms while keeping brief surges functional. We'll test that matrix (steady x burst_multiplier x burst_window).

Arjun (Eng-Infra): I'll spin up the staging experiment and post metrics (token_bucket occupancy, 429 rate, billing_retry_trigger). Planning 3 runs: no-burst limit, small-burst (x3, 5s), medium-burst (x5, 10s).

Maria (Support): Thanks — saving repro steps in the ticket and pinging BrightGrove contact. Followups here as we get results. :thumbsup:
